**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organization (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. You should write between 450 - 500 words. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity.

questions.enonce_markdown: **e)** Students should not do holiday jobs. Do you agree?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: state my position, I partly disagree, students may do holiday jobs.
2. Arguments for the other side: holidays are for rest, danger of abuse, danger of poor results.
3. My reasons: money, experience, discipline, independence.
4. Conditions: safe, legal, limited jobs.
5. Conclusion: restate my position.

**Model composition (459 words)**

Every year, when the school year ends, many students look for ways to spend their long vacation. Some travel to the village, others sit at home watching television, and a large number take a job in a shop, a bakery or a garage. Some people say that students should not do holiday jobs. In my opinion, this view is too strict, and I do not agree with it.

I understand the arguments of those who oppose holiday jobs. They say that the holiday is meant for rest, and that a student who has worked hard for nine months needs time to relax. They fear that employers may exploit young people by giving them heavy work for little pay. Some parents also worry that their children will enjoy money too much and lose interest in school. These fears are not without foundation, because there have been cases of students who were mistreated by their bosses or abandoned their studies for money.

Nevertheless, I believe that a well-chosen holiday job brings more advantages than disadvantages. First, it helps the student to earn money. In many Cameroonian families, parents struggle to pay school fees and buy books. A student who sells in a shop or works on a farm for two months can pay for his own uniform, his exercise books or even part of his fees, and thus reduce the burden on his parents.

Second, a holiday job gives practical experience that the classroom cannot give. A student who works in a pharmacy learns how to deal with customers and respect time, and a student who helps in a workshop learns to use his hands. Such skills will be very useful when he looks for a job after his studies, and some students even discover the career they wish to follow.

Third, working teaches discipline and responsibility. The student learns to wake up early, obey instructions, work with others and handle money carefully. He also learns to respect the dignity of labour, which is a precious lesson in a country where many young people dream of easy money. Finally, a job keeps young people busy, and so protects them from the bad habits that idleness often brings, such as gambling, drinking and bad company, which tempt those who have nothing to do.

Of course, some conditions must be respected. The job must be safe and legal, the student must not work too many hours, and he should keep a few weeks for rest and revision. Parents should also supervise the choice of the job and the employer.

In conclusion, holiday jobs should not be forbidden to students. If they are properly chosen and limited, they give money, experience and discipline, and prepare the student to become a hardworking and independent adult.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organization | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Not giving an opinion clearly (the topic asks 'Do you agree?').
2. Giving only one side of the argument with no reasons or examples.
